Alexandria. Medea’s love for Jason, for whom she procures magic potions that will give him
strength in Book III of that poem, is another model further to Aphrodite’s love for Anchises
in the Homeric Hymn To Aphrodite, of a goddess in danger of being afflicted by her passion
for mortals. A recent English literary source for Egyptianism was Clara Reeve, whose novel
The Old English Baron Claire read on 7 August (Claire Jnl 168). ‘The History of Charoba,
Queen of Aegypt’, an adaptation of a story based on Vattier’s Egyptian History, trans. John
Davies (1672), is printed with Reeve’s The Progress of Romance, 2 vols (1785). Charoba, only
